title: Canada Holds PR Target at 380,000, Opens Path for 200,000 Already There
excerpt: The 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan keeps admissions flat at 380,000 a year, but Budget 2026 adds a one-time transition to permanent residence for up to 200,000 temporary residents already in Canada by the end of 2027.
body:
• Canada will admit 380,000 permanent residents a year in each of 2027, 2028 and 2029, holding the target flat in the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan released with Budget 2026 on November 5.
  • The budget's one new opening is a one-time measure to transition up to 200,000 temporary residents already in Canada to permanent residence by the end of 2027 — 100,000 of them skilled workers through Express Entry and the Provincial Nominee Program.
  • New temporary resident arrivals stay capped at 370,000 a year, so anyone outside Canada faces the same tight intake as this year; no application route for the 200,000-person transition has been published yet.
  • Counting the top of the 2027 admissions range (422,000) plus the transition measure, CIC News calculates up to 622,000 people could become permanent residents in 2027 — but the annual target itself has not risen.

Canada is holding its immigration levels flat for three more years while opening a single, large door for people already inside the country. The 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, published with Budget 2026 on November 5, sets permanent resident admissions at 380,000 a year for 2027, 2028 and 2029, and new temporary resident arrivals at 370,000 a year, according to CIC News and a detailed breakdown by immigration.ca. Reuters, summarizing the budget tabled by Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne, reported the same two figures: 380,000 permanent resident admissions and 370,000 temporary resident arrivals in each of the next three years.

Who is affected

The plan touches three groups differently. Temporary residents already in Canada — workers and former students holding Canadian status — are the only group offered something new: a one-time transition to permanent residence for up to 200,000 people by the end of 2027. Prospective immigrants applying from abroad face an unchanged contest for the same 380,000 annual admissions. Prospective students and temporary workers abroad face an unchanged cap of 370,000 new arrivals a year, continuing the tighter intake of the past two years.

"Budget 2026 proposes $302.3 million over four years, starting in 2027–28, to implement the transition measure."

What changed, precisely

The headline targets did not move. Last year's 2026–2028 plan had already set 380,000 permanent resident admissions for 2027 and 2028 as notional figures; the new plan confirms them and extends the same level to 2029, immigration.ca reported. What is new is the transition measure. Of the up to 200,000 in-Canada transitions, 100,000 places are earmarked for skilled workers through Express Entry and the Provincial Nominee Program, in collaboration with the provinces and territories, according to the budget reporting by CIC News. The budget does not yet say who makes up the remaining 100,000, how candidates will be selected, or whether these admissions count inside the 380,000 annual target, immigration.ca noted. Budget 2026 proposes $302.3 million over four years, starting in 2027–28, to implement the transition measure.

CIC News reported that the plan breaks the 380,000 midpoint for each year into 244,700 economic admissions, 81,000 family reunification admissions, 49,300 refugees and protected persons, and 5,000 humanitarian and compassionate and other admissions, with a 2027 range of 352,500 to 422,000. It also reported temporary residence targets for 2027 of 220,000 foreign workers — 50,000 under the Temporary Foreign Worker Program, which requires a Labour Market Impact Assessment, and 170,000 under the LMIA-exempt International Mobility Program — and 150,000 international students. Targets for French-speaking admissions outside Quebec rise from 9.5 percent of admissions in 2027 to 10.5 percent in 2028 and 12 percent in 2029, CIC News reported. Program-level detail beyond the budget's overall targets is still to come when the immigration minister tables the 2026 Annual Report to Parliament on Immigration, immigration.ca said.

Where the 622,000 figure comes from

The larger number in early headlines is arithmetic, not a new target. Adding the top of the 2027 admissions range, 422,000, to the up to 200,000 transition places gives 622,000 potential new permanent residents in 2027, CIC News calculated. Separately, the remainder of last year's one-time initiatives — up to 115,000 protected persons and 33,000 in-Canada workers promised over 2026–2027 — is still to be admitted before the end of 2027; 46,330 people had been admitted under those initiatives from January to August 2026, according to CIC News. The levels themselves remain well below recent actuals: Canada admitted 483,655 permanent residents in 2024, and new international student arrivals between January and August 2026 were 71 percent lower than in the same period of 2024, immigration.ca reported.

What to do next

There is nothing to file yet. No eligibility criteria or application process for the transition measure have been published, and immigration.ca cautioned that applicants should not assume the measure will be counted the way last year's one-time initiatives were until Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada publishes the details. Workers and students already in Canada who hope to use the pathway should keep their current status valid and watch for the Annual Report to Parliament, which the budget says will carry the additional detail. The government's stated goal is to bring temporary residents below 5 percent of the population by the end of 2027 — the pressure that is shaping both the cap on new arrivals and the decision to regularize people already here.
